paper.title: Inner Monologue: Embodied Reasoning through Planning with Language Models
paper.central_claim: Feeding language-form environment feedback (success detection, passive object/scene description, active human/VQA answers) back into a frozen LLM planner over pretrained skills lets it retry, replan or ask, significantly improving instruction completion in simulated and real tabletop rearrangement and real kitchen mobile manipulation, especially under disturbances.

status_reason: full text with appendices A-D read; in-scope (frozen LLM planner with detector feedback over skills on real robots)

evidence.quote: We find that closed-loop language feedback significantly improves high-level instruction completion on three domains
evidence.support_explanation: central claim

evidence.quote: However, both approaches effectively produce the plan while assuming that each proposed step is executed successfully by the agent.
evidence.support_explanation: gap: SayCan/Huang plans are open-loop w.r.t. execution outcome

evidence.quote: by continually injecting information from the various sources of feedback into the LLM planning language prompts as the robot interacts with the environment
evidence.support_explanation: mechanism: textual feedback appended to the planner prompt

evidence.quote: Engineered success detectors can operate on ground-truth state in simulation, while learned success detectors can be trained on real examples of successes and failures in the real world
evidence.support_explanation: feedback channel privilege differs by domain

evidence.quote: Table 1: Success rates for various methods, averaged across 50 episodes in Ravens-based environment with test-time disturbances.
evidence.support_explanation: sim evaluation: 50 episodes per task cell
unseen-style task 'matching bowls' row: CLIPort 0, CLIPort+oracle 0, LLM+Object 56, +Success 70, +Scene 82 (column order inferred from header)
seen task 'Put all blocks in the [x] bowl': CLIPort+oracle 94 beats every Inner Monologue variant (46-56)
seen task 'Stack all the blocks': CLIPort+oracle 32 exceeds Inner Monologue variants (4-26)

evidence.quote: we assume access to oracle scene descriptors in the form of human observers or scripted systems to provide textual description back to the LLM planner
evidence.support_explanation: feedback sources are oracle/human in sim and kitchen
real tabletop total over two tasks x 10 runs: open-loop object 20, IM Object 45, IM Success 40, IM Object+Success 90 (columns inferred from header)

evidence.quote: we artificially inject Gaussian noise into the policy actions
evidence.support_explanation: failures are induced rather than natural
kitchen: SayCan 30.8, +Success 48.7, +Object+Success 60.4

evidence.quote: we add adversarial disturbances during control policy executions that cause skill policy rollouts to fail
evidence.support_explanation: disturbance protocol

evidence.quote: Without any LLM-informed feedback SayCan has success rate close to 0%
evidence.support_explanation: baseline cannot retry; large relative effect under forced failure

evidence.quote: We use human-provided object recognition to provide feedback about the presence of objects visible to the robot camera.
evidence.support_explanation: kitchen Object feedback is human-provided

evidence.quote: The success detector is built using heuristics based on ground-truth object poses
evidence.support_explanation: sim success detector uses simulator ground truth

evidence.quote: To allow for automatic evaluations, a binary reward function is defined for each task using ground-truth state of the objects.
evidence.support_explanation: sim outcome from ground truth, 50 episodes

evidence.quote: False negative predictions from the success detector lead to additional retry attempts, while false positive predictions add adversarial partial observability to the environment.
evidence.support_explanation: named failure modes

evidence.quote: In some instances, we found that the LLM planners ignored the environment feedback and still proposed policy skills involving objects not present in the scene.
evidence.support_explanation: planner may ignore feedback

evidence.quote: ViLD has strong overall accuracy, but still fails to detect objects 28.0% of the time.
evidence.support_explanation: automated object recognition measured on 10 episodes only

evidence.quote: We evaluate each method on four seen tasks and four unseen tasks, where seen tasks may be used for training
evidence.support_explanation: seen/unseen split for sim; seen tasks used as few-shot prompts

evidence.quote: The performance of low-level control policies limits not only overall high-level instruction completion performance
evidence.support_explanation: residue: skill bottleneck

evidence.quote: we report CLIPort evaluations with oracle termination (i.e., repeat until oracle indicates task completion) and fixed-step termination
evidence.support_explanation: baseline is a different, trained policy with oracle help

evidence.quote: we observe that they are of varying levels of consistency when no similar examples have been provided in the prompt
evidence.support_explanation: emergent behaviors are anecdotal

evidence.quote: as well as an open-loop variant that only runs object recognition once at the beginning of the task
evidence.support_explanation: open-loop one-shot description baseline (Socratic-style)

evidence.quote: Success Feedback Ground truth + heuristics MDETR + heuristics Finetuned CLIP
evidence.support_explanation: success detector source per domain: GT, MDETR heuristics, fine-tuned CLIP

evidence.quote: We implement Inner Monologue in a robotic system using the kitchen environment and task definitions described in SayCan [ 21 ] .
evidence.support_explanation: same kitchen/tasks/skills as SayCan baseline

evidence.quote: Socratic Models [ 19 ] combines several foundation models (e.g., GPT-3 [ 9 ] , ViLD [ 77 ] ) and language-conditioned policies
evidence.support_explanation: closest open-loop language-interface neighbor

evidence.quote: We evaluate methods on 120 evaluations over three task families
evidence.support_explanation: kitchen denominator; per-cell n not stated (percentages imply ~6-9)

signatures.object: Planner prompt as a growing dialogue of [robot action, feedback] over a pretrained skill library
signatures.information: instruction + after each skill: success flag, object list, task-progress sub-goals; privileges vary: simulator ground truth (sim), MDETR + box heuristics (real tabletop), fine-tuned CLIP success detector + human object list (kitchen)
signatures.operation: append feedback text after each skill; planner (InstructGPT 1.3B or PaLM 540B) emits next skill, retries, replans or stops
signatures.conditions: feedback expressible in text; skills callable by language; detector quality adequate
signatures.feedback: per-step success detection and scene description
signatures.selection_rule: LLM next-token choice (kitchen adds SayCan affordance weighting)
signatures.selection_data: few-shot prompts of 2-12 episodes per domain
signatures.persistence: prompt history within the episode only
signatures.claimed_effect: sim 56/70/82 vs open-loop; real tabletop 20->90%; kitchen 30.8->60.4%
signatures.failure_boundary: success-detector false negatives/positives, planner ignoring feedback, skill capability

signatures.information: after each step the LLM chooses 'continue' or 'ask'; answers are human-written in the case study
signatures.operation: LLM-generated question appended with the human reply

retention_trace.reason: no harness change is selected or persisted across tasks; only within-episode prompt history

gap.author_gap: LLM planners such as Huang et al. and SayCan emit plans assuming every step succeeds; they are not robust to intermediate failures, poor low-level policies or occluded scenes
gap.checked_gap: concrete and testable: SayCan with forced failures is close to 0% (E014) and one-shot object recognition misses occluded blocks (E025)

claims.text: feedback improves completion in simulated tabletop rearrangement, including unseen tasks
claims.setting: Ravens-based sim, 8 tasks x 50 episodes, noise injected
claims.baseline_control: CLIPort (+oracle termination), LLM with one-shot Object listing
claims.selection_vs_test: seen tasks serve as prompts; feedback derived from ground truth
claims.result: e.g. matching bowls 56 -> 70 -> 82; stacking on corners about 0-6 for all
counterevidence: CLIPort+oracle beats every IM variant on seen tasks (94 vs 46-56; 32 vs 4-26) (E007, E008)
claims.allowed_conclusion: with oracle feedback, closed-loop language feedback helps on long-horizon matching tasks and generalizes to unseen instructions; not uniformly better than a trained policy with a termination oracle

claims.text: closed-loop detection and description lets a real tabletop robot recover
claims.setting: UR5e, 2 tasks x 10 runs, injected action noise
counterevidence: success criterion for the evaluated task not defined in text
claims.allowed_conclusion: on two toy tasks with induced noise, combined feedback helps

claims.text: feedback improves a real mobile-manipulator kitchen agent over SayCan, especially under disturbances
claims.setting: 120 evaluations, 3 task families, with/without adversarial disturbance
claims.baseline_control: SayCan with the same LLM and skills
claims.allowed_conclusion: retry/replan with detector or human feedback outperforms SayCan on these forced-failure tasks

assessment.evidence_level_reason: closed-loop sim and real runs with counts; feedback in sim is privileged, kitchen object feedback is human, tasks overlap with prompts; no unseen embodiment, so not transfer (anchors precedent 1)
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: With oracle, scripted, learned or human feedback injected as text, a frozen LLM planner over pretrained skills recovers from induced failures better than the same planner without feedback in sim, a toy real tabletop and a real kitchen; it does not uniformly beat a trained policy with a termination oracle on seen tasks
assessment.author_claim_kept: closed-loop language feedback significantly improves instruction completion on three domains
unresolved: per-cell n and variance in the kitchen

G.reason: specific, falsifiable gap (plans assume step success), nearest neighbors are in the same experiment (SayCan baseline in the same kitchen, Socratic-style open-loop description), residue is stated (oracle feedback, skill bottleneck)

M.reason: feeding detector/description text to the planner directly addresses silent step failure and omitted occluded objects, with predicted complementarity of Success and Object tested; reliance on the LLM actually using feedback is only empirical and it sometimes ignores it

X.reason: three instantiations with detectors, thresholds, prompts and noise models are documented in Appendix A/D; conditions and failure modes (detector FP/FN, planner ignoring feedback, skill limits) are explicit; privileged/human channels and per-domain differences make the common pipeline only partly reproducible

measurement.reason: sim outcome from ground truth with 50 episodes per cell, but real tabletop success criterion is not defined, kitchen cell sizes are unstated (percentages imply about 6-9) and success judge is unspecified (anchors v2: undefined criterion or incomplete denominators cap at 2)

causality.reason: same-LLM/skill baseline (SayCan), open-loop description control and per-feedback toggles; counter-pattern: trained CLIPort+oracle wins on some seen tasks, Success lowers some cells, and oracle feedback is a privileged channel inflating the effect

holdout.reason: sim has seen/unseen task split and gains persist on unseen tasks, but feedback and scoring both read simulator ground truth (privileged, anchors precedent 1), real tabletop prompts include the evaluation tasks, one embodiment

statistics.reason: no variance or intervals, small unreported cell n in the kitchen (about 6-9 implied), 10 runs per tabletop task; failure causes appear in Fig. 4 whose content is not in the text material

cost.reason: no counts of extra LLM calls, tokens, latency, human interventions or detector compute; baseline and feedback variants are not budget-matched
